was in focus on Wednesday as Citi upped its earnings estimates on the memory maker, citing better-than-expected pricing for dynamic random access memory.

"We model F4Q26 sales/EPS of $51B/$31.45, above consensus of $50.8B/$31.43 and F1Q27 sales/EPS of $57B/$35.25, above consensus of $56.7B/$35.15," Citi analyst Atif Malik wrote in a note to clients. "We raise near-term NAND/DRAM pricing assumptions on non-SCA contracted bits. We assume blended DRAM ASPs +20%/+13% Q/Q and blended NAND ASPs +34%/+15% in F4Q/F1QE, respectively. We expect Micron volume/bits to grow roughly in line with the industry in 2026. We model FY27 capex of $50B with shell spend in low $20s and remaining equipment."
Malik reiterated his Buy rating on Micron and upped his price target to $1,300 from $1,150 with the revised earnings estimates.

The markets for DRAM and NAND are likely to remain "undersupplied" due to strong AI demand for the foreseeable future, Malik explained. However, he expects prices will start to decelerate over the next four quarters and peak in the second quarter of 2027.

title: Micron in focus as Citi ups estimates on better-than-expected DRAM pricing
